note.question: Why do ordinary social-media users produce content and follow one another reciprocally, and how can platforms encourage engagement without destroying the audience value that sustains production?
note.overview: A continuum of social-media users chooses unilateral follows and bilateral attention-bartering links. New links require both users' consent and existing bilateral links can be severed unilaterally, so every user's payoff and best response depend on the network formed by others; the paper explicitly defines and characterizes equilibrium.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Users choose bilateral attention-bartering relationships while anticipating optimal unilateral following. Conditional on the reciprocal network, each user unilaterally follows other users whose content yields positive consumption value. A new reciprocal relationship requires the prospective partner's consent, whereas either user may sever an existing reciprocal relationship unilaterally. Organic following is driven only by consumption value, whereas reciprocal following trades a consumption or monitoring cost for additional audience attention.
